issues.description: The method singFarmSong() has inconsistent return types across artifacts. The UML in the problem statement and the template Farm.java declare/expect singFarmSong() to be void and to print the song, but the solution implementation returns a String. This mismatch can confuse students about whether they should print the song directly (void) or build and return it (String), and may lead to failing tests or grading differences.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to match the problem/template: make singFarmSong() return void and print the song directly (using System.out.println) as described in the specification and UML. Alternatively, if returning the song text is intentional, update the UML and template method signature and the problem description to reflect a String return and update tests accordingly.

issues.description: The private helper singFarmSongVerse(...) has inconsistent return types. The UML and template define it as a void helper that prints the verse, while the solution implements it as a private method that returns a String. This structural difference in the helper's contract affects how students are expected to implement verse generation vs. printing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper consistent with the intended design. Either change the solution's singFarmSongVerse(Animal) to return void and perform printing (so it matches the UML/template), or update the template and problem statement to document that the helper should return a String and that singFarmSong will concatenate/return the full song text. Prefer keeping the helper void and printing to match the exercise description.
